title.zh: 卷一百〇八 表第九 外戚恩澤侯表
title.en: Volume 108 Tables 9: Families of the Imperial Consorts

sentences.zh: 古恩澤封有三，曰外戚，曰中官，曰嬖倖。

translations.literal: In antiquity grace-and-favor enfeoffments were of three kinds: called consort kin, palace eunuchs, and favorites.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times there were three kinds of grace-and-favor enfeoffment: consort kin, palace eunuchs, and imperial favorites.

sentences.zh: 明興，追崇外氏，廟貌之隆，爵超五等，而苗裔無攷，未及授官。

translations.literal: When Ming arose, they retroactively honored the maternal clans; temple grandeur was lofty and ranks exceeded the five grades, yet descendants had not been traced and offices had not yet been granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming dynasty was founded, the court retroactively honored the maternal clans with lofty temple rites and ranks above the five grades, but their descendants had not been traced and had not yet been given offices.

sentences.zh: 高后外家不奉朝請，家法之嚴有自來矣。

translations.literal: Empress Gao's maternal kin did not attend court audiences; the strictness of household law had long existed.
translations.idiomatic: The maternal kin of Empress Gao did not attend court audiences; the dynasty's strict household discipline in this regard was of long standing.

sentences.zh: 自文皇后而外，率由儒族單門，入儷宸極。

translations.literal: Apart from Empress Wen, all came from Confucian gentle families of humble lineage, entering to pair with the imperial apex.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from Empress Wen, empresses were generally drawn from scholarly families of modest standing who rose to share the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 后父初秩不過指揮，侯伯保傅以漸而進。

translations.literal: Fathers of empresses at first held no rank higher than commander; marquis, earl, tutor, and grand tutor advanced by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: At first an empress's father held no rank higher than military commander; only gradually was he advanced to marquis, earl, tutor, or grand tutor.

translations.literal: The favored received generous estates and fields, with ranks of servants and slaves.
translations.idiomatic: The more favored received ample estates and households of retainers and servants.

sentences.zh: 雖擁侈富之資，曾無憑藉之勢，制防之微意寓焉。

translations.literal: Although they possessed extravagant wealth, they never had a position to rely upon; the subtle intent of regulatory precaution lay therein.
translations.idiomatic: Though they enjoyed great wealth, they lacked any real power base—a subtle expression of the dynasty's preventive controls.

sentences.zh: 肅宗申明功令，裁抑世封，戚畹周親不得與汗馬餘勳為齒。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong clarified merit statutes, curtailed hereditary enfeoffments, and consort kin and close relatives could not be ranked with the remaining merit of sweating horses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong clarified the statutes on merit, curtailed hereditary enfeoffments, and barred consort kin and close royal relatives from standing on equal footing with battle-honored ministers.

translations.literal: Although called heart-and-liver kin, in practice they were inferior to enfeoffed lords.
translations.idiomatic: Though styled as the emperor's closest kin, in practice they ranked below enfeoffed nobles.

translations.literal: Compared with Han and Tang, they were nearly utterly disparate.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Han and Tang practice, the difference was almost complete.

sentences.zh: 茲考實錄所載封襲歲月，備列為表，以別於元功之次。

translations.literal: Here we examine the years of enfeoffment and succession recorded in the Veritable Records, set them forth fully in a table, and distinguish them from the order of founding merit.
translations.idiomatic: Here the years of enfeoffment and succession recorded in the Veritable Records are set out in full in tabular form, distinct from the order of founding merit.

sentences.zh: 他若宦官子弟濫列金貂，方士義兒均從班爵，騁文成之丕誕，踵養子之傾輈，亂政亟行，若循一軌，各依年次，備著於篇，亦班固表外戚，譜張釋、欒大之例也。

translations.literal: Elsewhere, eunuchs' sons recklessly ranked among those with golden cicada finials; Daoist masters' adopted sons alike followed court ranks; Wen Cheng's great absurdities were indulged, and the overturning of adopted sons was followed—misgovernment ran urgently as if along one track. Each is recorded by year in this chapter, following Ban Gu's table on consort kin and his cataloguing of Zhang Shi and Luan Da as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Likewise, eunuchs' sons were improperly listed among high court ranks, Daoist masters' adopted sons received noble titles, Wen Cheng's extravagances were indulged, and the abuse of adoptive succession recurred—misrule pursued a single course. Each case is recorded here in chronological order, following Ban Gu's precedent in tabulating consort kin and cataloguing Zhang Shi and Luan Da.

translations.literal: Adopted son of the inner attendant Cao Jixiang. In the twelfth month of Tianshun year 1 enfeoffed for Jixiang's merit in seizing the Gate. In the seventh month of year 5 he plotted rebellion and was executed.

translations.literal: Father of the Xianzong Emperor's mother, Empress Dowager Xiaosu. Posthumously enfeoffed on jiawu in the fourth month of Chenghua year 4. In the twelfth month of year 17 further posthumously made Duke of Ning, posthumous title Rongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Father of Empress Dowager Xiaosu, mother of the Xianzong Emperor. He was posthumously enfeoffed on jiawu in the fourth month of Chenghua 4, and in the twelfth month of year 17 was further posthumously made Duke of Ning with the title Rongjing.

translations.literal: Grandson of Empress Rui's younger brother Zhong. Enfeoffed on gengchen in the first month of Chenghua year 15. In the fourth month of Hongzhi year 2 granted hereditary succession. Died in the intercalary twelfth month of Jiajing year 4.

translations.literal: Father of the Guangzong Emperor's mother, Empress Dowager Xiaojing. Enfeoffed when Emperor Guangzong took the throne. Died in Chongzhen year 14.

translations.literal: Father of the Guangzong Emperor's Empress Xiaoyuan. On guichou in the ninth month of Taichang year 1 enfeoffed as earl. In the intercalary second month of Tianqi year 1 advanced to marquis.

cells.content: 熹宗母孝和太后弟。天啟元年閏二月封伯，尋進侯。崇禎八年卒。

translations.literal: Younger brother of the Xizong Emperor's mother, Empress Dowager Xiaohe. In the intercalary second month of Tianqi year 1 enfeoffed as earl, soon advanced to marquis. Died in Chongzhen year 8.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother of Empress Dowager Xiaohe, mother of the Xizong Emperor. He was enfeoffed as earl in the intercalary second month of Tianqi 1, soon raised to marquis, and died in Chongzhen 8.

translations.literal: Succeeded on wuyin in the twelfth month of Chongzhen year 9. Died at the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded on wuyin in the twelfth month of Chongzhen 9 and was killed by the rebels.

translations.literal: Father of the Xizong Emperor's empress. In Tianqi 1 enfeoffed as earl. In the eleventh month of Chongzhen year 11 advanced to marquis. Died at the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Father of the Xizong Emperor's empress. He was enfeoffed as earl in Tianqi 1, raised to marquis in the eleventh month of Chongzhen 11, and was killed by the rebels.

cells.content: 內臣魏忠賢姪。天啟六年三月封肅寧伯，進侯。十月戊申進封公。七年八月丙申加太師。莊烈帝即位，伏誅。

translations.literal: Nephew of the inner attendant Wei Zhongxian. In the third month of Tianqi year 6 enfeoffed as Earl of Suning, advanced to marquis. On wushen in the tenth month advanced to duke. On bingshen in the eighth month of year 7 made Grand Preceptor. When Emperor Zhuanglie took the throne, executed.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew of the eunuch Wei Zhongxian. When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended the throne, he was executed.

cells.content: 忠賢從孫。天啟七年七月己卯封。八月丙申加少師。莊烈帝即位，伏誅。

translations.literal: Zhongxian's younger cousin's grandson. Enfeoffed on jimao in the seventh month of Tianqi year 7. On bingshen in the eighth month made Junior Preceptor. When Emperor Zhuanglie took the throne, executed.

translations.literal: Liangqing's younger brother. Enfeoffed on yisi in the eighth month of Tianqi year 7. When Emperor Zhuanglie took the throne, executed.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother of Wei Liangqing. He was enfeoffed on yisi in the eighth month of Tianqi 7 and was executed when the Chongzhen Emperor ascended the throne.

cells.content: 莊烈帝母孝純太后弟。莊烈帝即位封。崇禎八年卒。九年，贈侯，予三代誥。十三年九月，父應元追封瀛國公。

translations.literal: Younger brother of the Zhuanglie Emperor's mother, Empress Dowager Xiaochun. Enfeoffed when Emperor Zhuanglie took the throne. Died in Chongzhen year 8. In year 9 posthumously advanced to marquis, granted patents for three generations. In the ninth month of year 13 his father Yingyuan was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Ying.

In the ninth month of year 13 his father Yingyuan was posthumously made Duke of Ying.

translations.literal: Succeeded on jiazi in the twelfth month of Chongzhen year 9. In the ninth month of year 13 made Junior Tutor. Died in hardship in the third month of year 17.

cells.content: 莊烈后父。崇禎三年封。十七年，京城陷，被執。

translations.literal: Father of the Zhuanglie Emperor's empress. Enfeoffed in Chongzhen year 3. In year 17, when the capital fell, he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Father of the Chongzhen Emperor's empress. He was enfeoffed in Chongzhen 3. When the capital fell in year 17, he was taken captive.
